docs.title: Stages
docs.text:
Stage Journal entry Triggered by Needs Rewards 10 I have reached the bridge to enter the town of Remgard. According to the bridge guard, the town is closed for outsiders to enter, and no-one is currently allowed to leave. They are investigating some disappearances of some of the townspeople. Bridge lookout (mountainlake13a) – – 15 I have offered my assistance in helping the people of Remgard investigate what has happened to the townspeople that have disappeared. Bridge lookout (mountainlake13a) – – 20 The bridge guard has asked me to investigate an abandoned house to the east along the northern shore of the lake. I should be wary of any inhabitants that may be there. Bridge lookout (mountainlake13a) – – 30 I have reported back to the bridge guard that I met Algangror in the abandoned house. Bridge lookout (mountainlake13a) – 3,000 XP 31 I have reported back to the bridge guard that the abandoned house was empty. Bridge lookout (mountainlake13a) – 3,000 XP 35 I have been granted entrance into Remgard. I should go visit Jhaeld, the town elder, to talk about what the next step should be. Jhaeld can probably be found in the tavern to the southeast. Bridge lookout (mountainlake13a) – – 40 Jhaeld was rather arrogant, but told me that they have had a problem with people disappearing for a while now. They have no clue what could be causing it. Jhaeld (remgard_tavern1) – – 50 I should visit four people in Remgard, and ask them about any clues on what might have happened to the missing people. Jhaeld (remgard_tavern1) – – 51 First is Norath, whose wife Bethir has disappeared. Norath can be found in the south-westernmost farmhouse. Jhaeld (remgard_tavern1) stage 50 – 52 Second, I should go talk to the Knights of Elythom, here in the tavern. Jhaeld (remgard_tavern1) stage 50 – 53 Third, I should go talk to the old woman Duaina in her house to the south. Jhaeld (remgard_tavern1) stage 50 – 54 Lastly, I should talk to Rothses, the armorer. He lives on the west side of town. Jhaeld (remgard_tavern1) stage 50 – 59 I tried to tell Jhaeld about Algangror, but he dismissed me as he had not heard me. Jhaeld (remgard_tavern1) stage 30, stage 50 – 61 I have talked to Norath. He and his wife had been fighting recently, but he has no idea on what may have happened to her. Norath (remgard_farmer3) stage 51 – 62 The Knights of Elythom in the Remgard tavern have had one of their knights disappearing recently. No one noticed anything when she disappeared, however. Krell (remgard_tavern0) stage 52 – 63 Duaina has seen me in her visions. I did not understand all that she spoke of, but the parts that were clear were that me and Andor were parts of a larger plot. I wonder what this means? She did not speak of any disappearing people however, not that I could understand anyway. Duaina (remgard3) stage 52 – 64 Rothses told me that Bethir visited him the night before she disappeared, to sell some equipment. He did not see where she went after that. Rothses (remgard_armour) stage 52 – 70 I have talked to all of the people that Jhaeld wanted me to talk to, but did not get any information from any of them about what may have happened to the missing people. I should go back to Jhaeld and ask what his plans are next. Norath (remgard_farmer3)Krell (remgard_tavern0)Duaina (remgard3)+1 more stage 51, stage 52, stage 61, stage 62, stage 63, stage 64 – 75 Jhaeld was really upset that I did not find out anything from the people that I was sent to talk to. Jhaeld (remgard_tavern1) – 15,000 XP 80 If I still want to help Jhaeld and the people of Remgard, I should look for clues in other places. (completes quest) Jhaeld (remgard_tavern1) – – 110 Jhaeld does not want to talk to me. I will not help them find out what happened to the missing people of Remgard. (completes quest) Jhaeld (remgard_tavern1) stage 50 –

Jhaeld (remgard_tavern1) – – 20 Jhaeld told me that he would rather not deal with her, since he believes she is very dangerous. Algangror (lonelyhouse0) – – 40 I have told Jhaeld that I defeated Algangror. Jhaeld (remgard_tavern1) hand over 1× Algangror's ring, stage 21, stage 35 – 41 Jhaeld was very pleased to hear the good news. The people of Remgard should now be safe, and the town can be opened to outsiders again. Jhaeld (remgard_tavern1) – – 45 For helping the people of Remgard find the cause of the disappearing people, Jhaeld told me to talk to Rothses. He might be able to improve some of my equipment. docs.text:
Every dialogue route found in the game data, including alternatives that end up in the same place. "Conditions" are everything checked along that dialogue path.

Stage 10: 1 route
  1. Talk to Aryfora (stoutford_gate) → choose “Don't worry about me. I can handle myself.” → stage 10. NPC: “Really? If you manage to do it, I'll make sure to reward you with something only I can do, and that I haven't done in…”
Stage 20: 1 route
  1. Talk to Caeda (lakecave2) → choose “Yes, Aryfora told me. She asked me to bring her some damerilias for Noraed's grave.” — conditions: reached stage 10 of The roots of love; NOT reached stage 20 of The roots of love; NOT reached stage 10 of A secret garden → stage 20; also gives 3× Damerilias. NPC: “I still have some. Here, take these to her, and send her my condolences.”
Stage 30: 1 route
  1. Talk to Aryfora (stoutford_gate) → choose “Yes. Here they are, three of the most beautiful damerilias.” — conditions: reached stage 10 of The roots of love; hand over 3× Damerilias → stage 30; also gives 1× Potion of deftness. NPC: “Oh. They're beautiful! Thank you! Here, take this potion as your reward.”
Stage 40: 1 route
  1. Talk to Aryfora (stoutford_gate) → choose “Caeda, Noraed's sister, gave them to me. She sends you her condolences.” — conditions: reached stage 30 of The roots of love → stage 40. NPC: “Noraed had a sister? He never talked about his family. He said he had a happy childhood, but that's it. I think he…”
Stage 45: 1 route
  1. Talk to Aryfora (stoutford_gate) → choose “I found them in the wild around Remgard.” — conditions: reached stage 30 of The roots of love → stage 45. NPC: “Is that so? Remgard must be a beautiful place to have such nice flowers growing in the wild.”

docs.title: Stages
docs.text:
Stage Journal entry Triggered by Needs Rewards 10 The priest in Stoutford looks scared of me and of what I did, but we never met before. Can this have something to do with Andor? Tahalendor (stoutford_church) – – 20 The priest's acolyte, Yolgen, told me that Andor was here a while ago, and since then, scary noises resonate in the church, seemingly coming from underground. Yolgen (stoutford_church) stage 10 – 25 A member of the Thieve's Guild in the tavern of Stoutford told me that the tavern owner dealt with Andor. Quiet thief (stoutford_tavern) stage 20 – 30 Glasforn, the owner of the tavern of Stoutford, admits to knowing Andor, but evades all my questions by boasting about his beds' quality.🔓 You can finally access a previously blocked area on Stoutford tavern. Glasforn (stoutford_tavern) stage 20 – 50 After sleeping in Glasforn's bed, I woke up in a cave, and was attacked by a monster. I killed it, but I should go see Glasforn again.👣 Reached by stepping onto a trigger spot on Stoutford cellar2.🔓 You can finally access a previously blocked area on Stoutford cellar2.🔓 You can finally access a previously blocked area on Stoutford cellar. stepping on a trigger on stoutford_cellar2 – changes map stoutford_tavern 60 When Glasforn saw me, he was really scared. Hopefully I'll get some information from him. Glasforn (stoutford_tavern) – – 70 I confronted Glasforn. He admited everything, but blamed Andor for it. How can Andor be involved in this? Glasforn (stoutford_tavern) stage 60 gives 1× Necklace of the Undead 80 Yolgen told me the rumbles have stopped. I should talk to the priest. Yolgen (stoutford_church) stage 50 – 85 The priest told me the monster was a lich. I should keep its heart safe. no trigger in the game data or code ? – – 90 The priest thanked me for saving his church and asked who the culprit was. Tahalendor (stoutford_church) carry 1× Demon heart, stage 80 gives Green apple, Bread, Major potion of health 100 I told him I do not know who was responsible. (completes quest) Tahalendor (stoutford_church) stage 90 2,000 XP 103 I told him Glasforn was responsible. (completes quest) Tahalendor (stoutford_church) stage 70, stage 90 2,500 XPremoves monsters from stoutford_tavern 106 I told him Andor was responsible. (completes quest) Tahalendor (stoutford_church) stage 70, stage 90 2,500 XP

docs.title: How each stage is reached
docs.text:
Every dialogue route found in the game data, including alternatives that end up in the same place. "Conditions" are everything checked along that dialogue path.

Stage 10: 2 routes
  1. Talk to Tahalendor (stoutford_church) → choose “What?” → stage 10. NPC: “Go away! You're not welcome here!”
  2. Talk to Tahalendor (stoutford_church) → choose “Actually, it's the first time we have met.” → stage 10. NPC: “Nonsense! Go away!”
Stage 20: 1 route
  1. Talk to Yolgen (stoutford_church) → choose “That must be my brother Andor!” — conditions: reached stage 10 of Rumblings → stage 20. NPC: “This church is the refuge for all the villagers when monsters attack. We are really worried now.”
Stage 25: 1 route
  1. Talk to Quiet thief (stoutford_tavern) → choose “Help me do what?” — conditions: reached stage 20 of Rumblings; reached stage 70 of Night visit → stage 25. NPC: “A kid that looked like you was here. He apparently did some business with the owner and the regulars.”
Stage 30: 1 route
  1. Talk to Glasforn (stoutford_tavern) → choose “Why?” — conditions: reached stage 20 of Rumblings → stage 30. NPC: “Well, you see, I keep some beds for occasions like this one. You can use the one in the corner, near the painting, if…”
Stage 50: 1 route
  1. stepping on a trigger on stoutford_cellar2 → the conversation leads here automatically — conditions: killed 1× Eliszylae; NOT reached stage 50 of Rumblings → stage 50; also changes map stoutford_tavern. NPC: “You hear a loud rumble, then nothing. Silence. What was that monster?”
Stage 60: 1 route
  1. Talk to Glasforn (stoutford_tavern) → the conversation leads here automatically — conditions: reached stage 60 of Rumblings → stage 60. NPC: “Wait. OK. I stand no chance against you. I'll tell you all I know.”
Stage 70: 1 route
  1. Talk to Glasforn (stoutford_tavern) → choose “I guess you are lucky I visited, although just asking me to kill it would have been easier. And nicer.” — conditions: reached stage 60 of Rumblings → stage 70; also gives 1× Necklace of the Undead. NPC: “I'm sorry! How was I to know you could actually kill it? You're just a kid! Anyway, now I can remove the necklace.…”
Stage 80: 1 route
  1. Talk to Yolgen (stoutford_church) → choose “Yes. I think I found the cause.” — conditions: reached stage 50 of Rumblings → stage 80. NPC: “Great. You should talk to my master. I told him you were not who he thought you were.”
Stage 90: 1 route
  1. Talk to Tahalendor (stoutford_church) → choose “These? You mean there are others?” — conditions: reached stage 80 of Rumblings; carry 1× Demon heart → stage 90; also gives Green apple, Bread, Major potion of health. NPC: “You know, since those monsters' attacks, we don't have much to offer, but take these. By the way, do you have any idea…”
Stage 100: 1 route
  1. Talk to Tahalendor (stoutford_church) → choose “Not really.” — conditions: reached stage 90 of Rumblings → stage 100. NPC: “It's a shame we cannot punish the culprits. Thank you for your help kid.”
Stage 103: 1 route
  1. Talk to Tahalendor (stoutford_church) → choose “It was all Glasforn's doing. The tavern owner.” — conditions: reached stage 90 of Rumblings; reached stage 70 of Rumblings → stage 103; also removes monsters from stoutford_tavern. NPC: “That fool! We'll make him pay. Thank you for your help kid.”
Stage 106: 1 route
  1. Talk to Tahalendor (stoutford_church) → choose “It was my brother Andor. I need to find him.” — conditions: reached stage 90 of Rumblings; reached stage 70 of Rumblings → stage 106. NPC: “That is troublesome. I have no idea where he went when he left Stoutford, but Kazaul has always been linked to the…”

Verified against v0.8.18 dialogue data.

Stage Journal entry Triggered by Needs Rewards 10 I met Borvis on the great road near Alynndir's hut. (completes quest) Borvis (galmore_41) – 1 XP 30 Since I aided the Shadow once or twice earlier, he requested my further help for an urgent task. Borvis (galmore_41) – – 40 He wanted me to investigate something bad in the Purple Hills in the weird areas to the south of Stoutford. Borvis (galmore_41) – sets stage 3 of Darkness in the Daylight and Shadows - Non displayed (hidden flag)spawns monsters on galmore_45 50 I went to the area to the south of Stoutford, and encountered an impassable force there. walking into a blocked passage on galmore_45 stage 40 – 60 There were strange glowing, immovable pebbles there. I had to inform Borvis. walking into a blocked passage on galmore_45 stage 40, stage 50 – 70 Borvis told me that was the basic, but effective, Shadow shield, to protect Shadow incantations from outside interference. Borvis (galmore_41) stage 60 – 80 For that, he would give me a chant. But I had to get him energies in the form of four 'blessings' - Shadow's Strength, Shadow Awareness, Fatigue, and Life Drain - within myself. He told me to go to Talion in Loneford for the first blessing, and for information about the others. Borvis (galmore_41) – – 90 Talion bestowed me with Shadow's Strength. Talion have 300 gold, pay 300 gold, stage 100 applies condition shadowbless_str 100 Talion told me to seek out Jolnor in Vilegard for the rest of the 'blessings'. Talion stage 90 – 110 Jolnor bestowed me with Shadow Awareness. Favlon (nw_sullengard_1) carry 10× Cooked meat, hand over 10× Cooked meat applies condition fatigue1applies condition life_drain 150 After a grueling travel back, I returned to Borvis. Borvis (galmore_41) – applies condition shadowbless_strapplies condition shadowsleepapplies condition fatigue1applies condition life_drain 165 Borvis told me to hurry back to the barrier. docs.text:
Every dialogue route found in the game data, including alternatives that end up in the same place. "Conditions" are everything checked along that dialogue path.

Talk to Godfrey (sullengard_inn) → choose “I'll take it, but I have to say that you really should join the Thieves' Guild with that attitude!” — conditions: NOT reached stage 1 of sullengard_nondisplay (hidden flag); pay 700 gold → stage 1. NPC: “Thank you! It pays to be the owner. You can use any available bed.”
Stage 2: 1 route
  1. stepping on a trigger on sullengard_tavern → choose “I would like to see what you have for sale.” → stage 2. NPC: “Certainly. I have a menu of the best beers found in not just Sullengard, but in all of Dhayavar.”
Stage 3: 1 route
  1. stepping on a trigger on sullengard_tavern → choose “Oh, but I will.” — conditions: reached stage 2 of sullengard_nondisplay (hidden flag); carry 1× Brimhaven brew; NOT reached stage 120 of sullengard_nondisplay (hidden flag) → stage 3. NPC: “Get out of here now. Do not come back until you learn some respect.”

  1. Talk to Deebo (sullengard_apple_farm_east) → choose “I am ready! No more talking.” — conditions: NOT reached stage 50 of Hunting the hunter; latest stage of Hunting the hunter is 0; NOT reached stage 4 of sullengard_nondisplay (hidden flag); random chance (30%) → stage 4; also sets stage 10 of Hunting the hunter. NPC: “The Golden jackal was last seen heading back into the "Sullengard forest" just to the west of my orchard. Return to me…”
Stage 5: 1 route
  1. stepping on a trigger on sullengard_woods14 → choose “Sure, why not? What could go wrong?” — conditions: NOT reached stage 5 of sullengard_nondisplay (hidden flag) → stage 5; also gives 1× Gloriosa mushroom

  1. Talk to Grazia (way_to_sullengard_east4_bridge) → choose “I will go first and you can follow close behind. Sound OK with you?” → stage 17. NPC: “Yes. Thank you.”

  1. Hence my reason for asking you about it.” — conditions: NOT reached stage 25 of sullengard_nondisplay (hidden flag); latest stage of Recovering stolen property is 30 → stage 25. NPC: “I wish I knew more, but I don't. Maybe ask around near the tavern?”

  1. stepping on a trigger on home → choose “Some of them were ants..” — conditions: reached stage 100 of Search for Andor; NOT reached stage 110 of Search for Andor; NOT reached stage 26 of sullengard_nondisplay (hidden flag); NOT reached stage 1 of ratdom_nondisplay (hidden flag) → stage 26. NPC: “$playername, I'm not laughing.”

  1. stepping on a trigger on sullengard_woods6 → the conversation leads here automatically — conditions: NOT reached stage 27 of sullengard_nondisplay (hidden flag) → stage 27. NPC: “[Looking around you, you can't help to be amazed at the giant trees that surround you.]”

How?” — conditions: reached stage 51 of Search for Andor; latest stage of Another ruthless Crackshot is 70; NOT reached stage 30 of sullengard_nondisplay (hidden flag); NOT reached stage 28 of sullengard_nondisplay (hidden flag) → stage 28; also gives 1000× Gold coins.   1. stepping on a trigger on way_to_sullengard_east4_bridge → the conversation leads here automatically → stage 29

NPC: “Thank you so much again, kid. You are just like your brother Andor. After we are done speaking, you really should…”

  1. Talk to Frosty (sullengard1) → the conversation leads here automatically → stage 31. NPC: “Roar!”
Stage 32: 1 route
  1. Talk to Tharwyn (vilegard_tavern) → choose “Let's get back to discussing your 'business agreement' with the 'distributors'.” — conditions: reached stage 30 of Trusting an outsider; reached stage 32 of sullengard_nondisplay (hidden flag); NOT reached stage 30 of Beer Bootlegging → stage 32. docs.title: Stages
docs.text:
Stage Journal entry Triggered by Needs Rewards 10 On the road between Loneford and Brimhaven, I found a dried up lake-bed with a major cavern below. Deep inside the cavern, I met Ulirfendor - a priest of the Shadow from Brimhaven. Ulirfendor is trying to translate the inscriptions on a shrine of Kazaul, and has determined that it speaks of the 'Dark protector', but he is unsure what that refers to. Whatever it means, he is determined that it must be stopped. Ulirfendor (waytobrimhavencave4) stage 15 – 11 Ulirfendor needs help with figuring out what some of the missing parts on the shrine says. The inscription reads 'Kulauil hamar urum Kazaul'te', but the next parts have been completely eroded from the rock. Ulirfendor (waytobrimhavencave4) stage 15 – 15 I have agreed to help Ulirfendor find out what the missing parts of the inscription might be. Ulirfendor believes the shrine speaks of a powerful creature that lives deeper inside the dungeon. Maybe that could provide some clue as to what the missing parts are. Ulirfendor (waytobrimhavencave4) – – 20 Deep inside the dungeon, I encountered a radiant guardian, guarding some other being. The guardian uttered the phrases 'Kulauil hamar urum Kazaul'te. Kazaul hamat urul'. This must be what Ulirfendor was looking for. I should return to him at once. Radiant guardian (waytobrimhavencave3a) stage 15 – 21 I tried to attack the guardian, but was unable to even reach it. Some powerful force held me back. Maybe Ulirfendor knows more. Radiant guardian (waytobrimhavencave3a) stage 32 – 30 Ulirfendor was very pleased to hear that I uncovered the missing parts of the inscription. Ulirfendor (waytobrimhavencave4) stage 15, stage 20 2,000 XP 32 He also told me the continuation of the inscription, but did not know what it means. I should go back to the guardian and speak the words that Ulirfendor told me. Ulirfendor (waytobrimhavencave4) – – 42 I have spoken the words to the guardian. Radiant guardian (waytobrimhavencave3a) stage 32 5,000 XP 45 The guardian gave off a chilling laughter, and started attacking me. Radiant guardian (waytobrimhavencave3a) – – 50 I defeated the guardian and reached the lich 'Toszylae'. The lich managed to infect me with something. I must kill the lich and return to Ulirfendor. Toszylae (waytobrimhavencave3a) – applies condition rotwormsets stage 10 of I have it in me 60 Ulirfendor told me that he had managed to translate the parts of the inscription that I told the guardian. Apparently, what I told the guardian roughly means 'My body for Kazaul'. Ulirfendor was very concerned about what this means for me, and was very regretful that he had made me speak the words. Ulirfendor (waytobrimhavencave4) – – 70 Ulirfendor was very happy to hear that I managed to defeat the lich. With the lich defeated, the people in the surrounding areas should be safe now. (completes quest) Ulirfendor (waytobrimhavencave4) stage 60 20,000 XP

docs.title: Stats & Skills
docs.text:
How your hero's numbers actually work in v0.8.18, pulled straight from the game's source code rather than from forum folklore. Click a heading to fold it away. Wondering what to do with all this? That's what Strategy is for.

Starting stats (level 1) Stat Lv 1 Stat Lv 1 Max HP 25 Critical skill 0 Max AP 10 Critical multiplier – Attack chance 60 Attack cost 4 AP Attack damage 1–1 Move cost 6 AP Block chance 9 Use item cost 5 AP Damage resistance 0 Re-equip cost 5 AP Levelling up Choice each level-up Bonus Max health +5 HP Attack chance +5 Attack damage +1 min & max Block chance +3

Pick one per level-up. There's no respec, so choose like you mean it. These picks form your base stats, which are the only values skill requirements look at. Gear and skills don't count, however shiny.

Skill points: levels 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36, 40, 44, 48, 52, 56, 60. That's 12 by level 50, and every one of them will feel like a hard decision. Experience: level L → L+1 costs 55 × L². Quadratic growth, so the grind gets real.

One point of Fortitude at level 5 out-earns a health level-up by level 10. Add a second level at 20 and it matches nine health level-ups by level 35, while those nine level-ups were free to go into other stats. Details on Strategy.

Level Total XP XP to next 2 55 220 5 1,650 1,375 10 15,675 5,500 15 55,825 12,375 20 135,850 22,000 25 269,500 34,375 30 470,525 49,500 40 1,129,700 88,000 50 2,223,375 137,500 60 3,861,550 198,000 How combat works

Every attack goes through the same four steps. No hidden dice, no secret modifiers; this is the whole thing. The stat glossary explains each stat.

1 · Hit? hit % = 50 × (1 + (2/π) × arctan((AC − BC − 50) / 40))

AC − BC Hit +5 AC adds -50 12% +0.6% +0 21% +1.7% +25 32% +3.0% +50 50% +4.0% +75 67% +2.7% +100 78% +1.5% +150 87% +0.5% +200 91% +0.3% +300 94% +0.1%

2 · Damage: random between min and max attack damage.

3 · Critical? Only if you have critical skill above 0 and a critical multiplier, which comes from your weapon (or from Way of the Monk when fighting unarmed). No multiplier, no crits, no matter how much critical skill you pile up. Ghosts, constructs and demons are immune either way. crit % = −5 + 2 × √(5 × critical skill), then damage × multiplier.

Crit skill Crit % 5 5% 10 9% 20 15% 30 19% 45 25% 60 29% 80 35% 100 39% 150 49%

4 · Armor: the target's damage resistance is subtracted from the result, with a floor of 0. Yes, a hit can do zero damage, and yes, it's as annoying as it sounds.

Attacks per turn = max AP ÷ attack cost, rounded down.

docs.title: Fighting style: Dual wield
docs.text:
Gives benefits when fighting with two weapons at the same time, one in the main hand and one in the off-hand.

Category Specialty Max level 2 Obtained via Skill points Unlocks Specialization: Dual wield

docs.title: Effect
docs.text:
Gives benefits when fighting with two weapons at the same time, one in the main hand and one in the off-hand.

Without this skill, only 25 % of a weapon's qualities may be used when equipped in the off-hand. This includes attack chance, critical skill, damage potential and block chance. Without this skill, attack cost (AP cost) of making an attack is the sum of the attack cost of the main weapon and that of the weapon used in the off-hand. The lower of both damage modifiers will be used.

With one level of this skill, 50 % of the off-hand's weapon's qualities may be used, and the attack cost is the highest attack cost of both weapons plus 50 % of the lowest attack cost of both weapons. The average of both damage modifiers will be used.

With two levels of this skill, 100 % of the off-hand's weapon's qualities may be used, and the attack cost equals the highest of the attack costs of the two equipped weapons. The highest damage modifier will be used.

docs.title: Stat glossary
docs.text: What each stat actually does in v0.8.18. Starting values live on Stats & Skills.

docs.title: Max HP
docs.text: Your health. Hit 0 and you're done. Raised by the max health level-up (+5), by Fortitude (+1 per skill level on every later level-up), and by some gear. Most experienced players get theirs almost entirely from Fortitude; see Strategy for why.

docs.title: Max AP
docs.text: Action points per combat turn. Attacking, moving and drinking potions all cost AP, and running out mid-fight is a classic way to die. Combat Speed adds +1 per level, up to 2.

docs.title: Attack chance
docs.text: Your accuracy. It's compared with the target's block chance to decide whether you hit, through a curve with heavy diminishing returns at both ends (details). Raised by the attack chance level-up (+5), Weapon Accuracy (+12 per level), weapons and proficiencies.

docs.title: Attack damage
docs.text: Each hit rolls a random number between your minimum and maximum damage. The attack damage level-up adds +1 to both. Hard Hit adds +2 to the maximum only, which sounds better than it is: your average goes up by just 1.

docs.title: Block chance
docs.text: Your evasion: the same curve as attack chance, pointed the other way. Raised by the block chance level-up (+3), Dodge (+9 per level), shields and armor. Only level-up block chance counts toward skill requirements like Bark Skin, so your fancy shield doesn't help there.

docs.title: Damage resistance
docs.text: Subtracted from every hit you take, after critical multipliers. Damage can't go below 0, so it shines against monsters that nibble at you with lots of small hits and does much less against ones that hit like a truck. Raised by Bark Skin (+1 per level), shields and armor.

docs.title: Critical skill
docs.text: Sets your critical hit chance: −5 + 2 × √(5 × critical skill). The square root means each extra point helps less than the one before. It does nothing unless you also have a critical multiplier (from your weapon, or Way of the Monk). More Criticals raises it by 20% per level.

docs.title: Critical multiplier
docs.text: How hard a critical hit lands (e.g. ×2). Weapons provide it. Bare fists have none, so unarmed heroes can't crit at all, unless they learn Way of the Monk, which grants ×1.25 per level. Better Criticals raises it by 25% per level.

docs.title: Attack cost
docs.text: AP spent per attack: 4 unarmed, or whatever your weapon says. Attacks per turn = max AP ÷ attack cost, rounded down, so a single point here can be worth an entire extra attack every turn, or absolutely nothing.

docs.title: Move cost
docs.text: AP to move one tile during combat. Heavy armor raises it, which is the price of looking like a walking tank.

docs.title: Use item cost
docs.text: AP to use an item, e.g. drinking a potion in the middle of a fight.

docs.title: Re-equip cost
docs.text: AP to change equipment during combat. Possible, but rarely a good use of your turn.

docs.title: Taunt
docs.text:
When an attacker makes an attack that misses, there is a 75 % chance that the attacker loses 2 action points (AP).

Category Defense Max level 1 Obtained via Skill points

docs.title: Effect
docs.text: When an attacker makes an attack that misses, there is a 75 % chance that the attacker loses 2 action points (AP). This applies to all types of melee attacks against you.

docs.title: Strategy
docs.text:
Advice on getting the most out of your hero. Unlike the rest of this wiki, these pages are written by hand. The numbers come straight from the game's code (v0.8.18); the opinions are just opinions. If you disagree, you might even be right.

  • Levelling & skill pointsWhere your level-ups and your painfully scarce skill points should go, and when.
  • Combat tipsAccuracy, armor, crits and attacks per turn, plus how to stop hitting armored monsters for 0.

docs.title: Combat tips
docs.text:
Written for v0.8.18. The formulas behind these tips are on Stats & Skills.

Read the monster's page before a hard fight

Every monster page lists its attack chance, block chance, damage resistance, attack cost and class. Ten seconds of reading beats a trip back to the last resting spot. Three numbers decide most fights:

  • Its block chance vs. your attack chance. If you're not at least ~50 above it, expect to whiff. A lot.
  • Its damage resistance vs. your damage. If its damage resistance is close to your minimum damage, many of your hits will do roughly nothing.
  • Its class. Ghosts, constructs and demons are immune to critical hits.
Accuracy: aim for a gap of 50–100

Hit chance follows an S-curve on the gap between your attack chance and the target's block chance:

Gap Hit chance 0 21% 50 50% 100 78% 150 87% 200 91%

Going from a 50 gap to 100 buys about 28 points of hit chance. Going from 150 to 200 buys about 4. Once you're 100+ ahead of what you usually fight, more accuracy is mostly decoration, and damage or defense will do more for you.

Armor punishes small hits

The target's damage resistance comes off every hit. Against 10 damage resistance, a weapon hitting for 8–12 does 0–2 per hit, while one hitting for 20–25 does 10–15. Against heavily armored enemies, bring your hardest-hitting weapon, even if it swings less often. A dagger build against a high-armor monster is a long, sad afternoon.

It works the other way too: your own damage resistance (Bark Skin, shields, armor) is at its best against monsters that pepper you with lots of small hits.

Attacks per turn: look for breakpoints

Attacks per turn = max AP ÷ attack cost, rounded down. You start with 10 AP, and Combat Speed adds up to 2 more:

Attack cost 10 AP 11 AP 12 AP 2 5 5 6 3 3 3 4 4 2 2 3 5 2 2 2 6 1 1 2

So Combat Speed is either a massive upgrade or two wasted skill points, depending entirely on your weapon. With a 5-AP weapon, both levels give you exactly nothing.1 The Jewel of Fallhaven (attack cost −1, sold by the tailor in Fallhaven) works the same way: check whether it actually tips you over a breakpoint before handing over the gold.

Crits need the right weapon and the right target

Critical skill does nothing without a critical multiplier. That comes from your weapon (check its page), or from Way of the Monk if you fight unarmed. Crit chance also has diminishing returns: 20 critical skill gives 15%, and you need 80 to reach 35%. And against ghosts, constructs and demons, crits simply don't happen, so a crit-focused hero should carry a plan B for those fights. "Hit it harder" is not a plan B.

  1. The leftover AP isn't completely useless, since you can spend it on moving or using items. But you didn't spend two skill points to walk around more. ↩

docs.title: Levelling & skill points
docs.text:
Written for v0.8.18. The mechanics behind all this are on Stats & Skills.

The short version (for the impatient)
  • Almost never pick max health at level-up. Take Fortitude at level 5 instead.
  • Hold your level-4 skill point for one level so it can go into Fortitude.
  • Put 2 early level-ups into block chance so Bark Skin is ready at level 10.
  • Spend the rest on attack chance and attack damage, leaning harder into damage as the game goes on.
  • Plan skill points backwards from the skills you want. The big ones are level-gated, and there's no respec.
Why Fortitude beats the max health level-up

The max health level-up gives +5 HP, once. Fortitude gives +1 HP on every level-up after you learn it, per skill level. It isn't retroactive, so the earlier you take it, the more it pays:

Fortitude level Earliest level Extra HP by level 50 Equal to this many health level-ups 1 5 +45 9 2 20 +30 6 3 35 +15 3

One skill point at level 5 ends up worth nine health level-ups, and those nine level-ups are now free to go into stats that skills can't replace. That's the whole reason "never level health" is the standard advice. It's not a meme; it's arithmetic.1

The catch: your first skill point shows up at level 4, but Fortitude won't let you in until level 5. Do not spend that level-4 point on something else. Your future self will send angry letters. Just hold it for one level.

Bonus: Fortitude also counts toward Regeneration, which needs Fortitude plus 30 base max HP per Regeneration level. Start at 25 HP, take Fortitude at 5, and you hit 30 base HP at level 10 without ever touching the health level-up.

Block chance and Bark Skin

Bark Skin gives +1 damage resistance per level, up to 5. Each level wants character level 10 × its level and base block chance of 15 × its level, and only block chance from level-ups counts. You start at 9, and each block chance level-up gives +3:

Bark Skin level Character level Base block chance Block chance level-ups needed (total) 1 10 15 2 2 20 30 7 3 30 45 12 4 40 60 17 5 50 75 22

Level 1 is a bargain: two block chance level-ups before level 10 and you're in. After that, each level costs five more level-ups and a skill point, which gets expensive fast. Decide early how far you're going instead of discovering at level 30 that you're one level-up short. Block chance also has few other sources (Dodge, shields, armor), so a stray block chance level-up here and there is rarely wasted.

Attack chance vs. attack damage
  • Attack chance (+5 per level-up) lives on the hit-chance curve. It's great while you're around 50 above the enemy's block chance and close to pointless once you're far ahead. It matters most early, before gear and weapon proficiencies start handing out accuracy for free. If you fall behind later, Weapon Accuracy gives +12 per skill point.
  • Attack damage (+1 to min and max per level-up) never goes out of style. Every point is one more damage on every single hit, and against armored enemies that's the difference between "chip damage" and "no damage". Lean into it more and more as the game goes on.
Skill point timeline

You get a skill point at levels 4, 8, 12 and so on: 12 by level 50, which is not a lot.2 Most of the good skills have level gates, so plan backwards:

Goal Earliest level Notes Fortitude 1 5 The held level-4 point. Bark Skin 1 10 Needs 2 block chance level-ups. Combat Speed 1 / 2 15 / 30 +1 max AP each. Check your weapon's attack cost first (why). A fighting style, levels 1 / 2 15 / 30 Dual wield, two-handed, or weapon & shield. Way of the Monk 1 / 2 / 3 15 / 30 / 45 Fists only, no armor. A lifestyle choice. Internal Bleeding 20 5 points: More Criticals 2 + Better Criticals 2 + itself. Fracture 40 10 points: More Criticals 4 + Better Criticals 4 + Internal Bleeding + itself. A specialization 45 Needs the matching fighting style at level 2.

The crit skills do nothing without a critical multiplier (a crit weapon, or Way of the Monk for unarmed heroes), and ghosts, constructs and demons ignore crits completely. Don't sink 10 points into the crit chain unless you have a crit weapon you plan to marry.

  1. The one real exception is a very early, very dangerous stretch where +5 HP right now matters more than +45 HP eventually. Even then, most players just grit their teeth and drink potions. ↩

  2. For comparison, you get 49 level-ups by level 50. Level-ups are cheap; skill points are not. Spend accordingly. ↩
